summary_hint: IRS Form 1098 (tax year <tax_year>) from <lender_name> for <borrower_name>: Box 1 interest <mortgage_interest_received>, Box 2 principal <outstanding_mortgage_principal>, property <property_address>.

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — the payer/borrower; match to the borrower

typed_core.name: borrower_address
typed_core.why: identity — the borrower's address (Box 7 compares the property address to this)
typed_core.prompt_hint: PAYER'S/BORROWER'S street address, city, state, ZIP

typed_core.name: borrower_tin_masked
typed_core.why: PII — the payer/borrower's TIN (SSN/ITIN), shown PRE-MASKED on the form (last 4 only)
typed_core.prompt_hint: PAYER'S/BORROWER'S TIN — capture the LAST 4 digits ONLY, exactly as shown (the form prints e.g. '*****7007'); never a full SSN

typed_core.name: lender_name
typed_core.why: identity — the recipient/lender (servicer)

typed_core.name: lender_address
typed_core.why: identity — the lender's address
typed_core.prompt_hint: RECIPIENT'S/LENDER'S street address, city, state, ZIP

typed_core.name: lender_tin
typed_core.why: identity — the recipient/lender's TIN, an EIN (a BUSINESS identifier, NOT personal PII). Kept UNMASKED and readable (LP-457: masking the employer EIN broke IN-5's equivalent); a hyphenated EIN (XX-XXXXXXX) has no 9-contiguous-digit run so it does not trip the at-rest guard
typed_core.prompt_hint: RECIPIENT'S/LENDER'S TIN (the lender's EIN, e.g. '26-1193089') — capture VERBATIM, do NOT mask (it is a business tax id, not personal PII)

typed_core.name: lender_phone
typed_core.why: processor — the servicer's contact phone

typed_core.name: account_number
typed_core.why: PII — the account/loan number the lender assigned (shown FULL on the form; = the servicer's Loan Number). Masked at the snapshot boundary; its value-hash joins the 1098 to the same loan's mortgage_statement / note
typed_core.prompt_hint: The 'Account number' (= Loan Number), captured VERBATIM/full; masked + hashed at the snapshot boundary

typed_core.name: tax_year
typed_core.why: identity — the calendar/tax year the statement covers

typed_core.name: mortgage_interest_received
typed_core.why: DT-6 — Box 1 mortgage interest received; evidences the housing expense on the (often retained) property

typed_core.name: outstanding_mortgage_principal
typed_core.why: DT-6 — Box 2 outstanding mortgage principal (the debt balance on the property)

typed_core.name: mortgage_origination_date
typed_core.why: processor — Box 3 mortgage origination date

typed_core.name: refund_of_overpaid_interest
typed_core.why: processor — Box 4 refund of overpaid interest

typed_core.name: mortgage_insurance_premiums
typed_core.why: processor — Box 5 mortgage insurance premiums (MIP/PMI)

typed_core.name: points_paid_on_purchase
typed_core.why: processor — Box 6 points paid on purchase of principal residence

typed_core.name: property_address_same_as_borrower_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — Box 7 indicator (checked when the property address equals the borrower's; unchecked when Box 8 carries a different address)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Box 7 checkbox — 'checked' or 'unchecked' (unchecked when Box 8 is completed with a different address)

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — Box 8 the property securing the mortgage; when it differs from the borrower address the property is retained/non-owner-occupied (the DT-6 case)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Box 8 'Address or description of property securing mortgage'

typed_core.name: number_of_properties
typed_core.why: processor — Box 9 number of properties securing the mortgage
typed_core.prompt_hint: Box 9 (may be blank if one property)

typed_core.name: other_information
typed_core.why: DT-6 — Box 10 free-text 'Other information'; servicers commonly print 'Real Estate Taxes Paid $N' here (the housing-expense taxes), but the content varies
typed_core.prompt_hint: Box 10 'Other' — capture the text VERBATIM as printed (e.g. 'Real Estate Taxes Paid $1,889.75'); do NOT parse it into a number

typed_core.name: mortgage_acquisition_date
typed_core.why: processor — Box 11 mortgage acquisition date (when the lender acquired the loan mid-year)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Box 11 — often blank; leave null if not printed

rejected.name: property_taxes_paid (parsed from Box 10)
rejected.reason: ⚠️ Box 10 is FREE TEXT ('Other information') — a servicer may print real-estate taxes, insurance-from-escrow, or anything. Parsing it into a typed property_taxes_paid Decimal is the is_disputed lesson: a field that looks like a clean value but holds free text will misfire. Capture Box 10 verbatim as other_information; a rule/reasoner interprets it. Tags describe; rules judge.

rejected.name: annual_housing_expense / total_housing_cost
rejected.reason: a COMPUTED figure (interest + taxes + insurance) — a judgment for a rule (DT-6), not a value on the form.

rejected.name: is_investment_property / is_owner_occupied
rejected.reason: a JUDGMENT inferred from Box 8 ≠ borrower address — the fact (the two addresses) is captured; the occupancy conclusion is a rule's call.

rejected.name: form_number / form_revision_date / omb_number
rejected.reason: the form is identified by classification; these are boilerplate — catch-all.

rejected.name: corrected_indicator
rejected.reason: the 'CORRECTED (if checked)' box is unchecked on both samples; low value — catch-all if ever set.

encoding_variations: Form 1098 is a fixed-box IRS form (like the W-2) — Boxes 1-11 in fixed positions; a servicer cover page ('Annual Tax and Interest Statement') may precede the form and repeat the loan number / customer service phone
the borrower TIN is PRE-MASKED on the form (last 4 only, e.g. '*****7007') — the full TIN is never printed
the account number is shown FULL (= the servicer loan number)
Box 10 'Other' is free text — commonly 'Real Estate Taxes Paid $N', but varies by servicer
Box 8 property address may differ from the borrower address (a retained/non-owner-occupied property) or match it (Box 7 checked instead)
Box 11 (mortgage acquisition date) is blank unless the lender acquired the loan mid-year

open_questions.q: Parse Box 10 into a typed property_taxes_paid field?
options: capture Box 10 verbatim as free text
parse the taxes into a Decimal
open_questions.recommendation: VERBATIM (GEET'S DECISION, LP-469): Box 10 is free text whose content varies by servicer; a typed taxes field would misfire (the is_disputed lesson). A rule/reasoner interprets other_information.

notes: ⚠️ GENUINE RULE TIE, not visibility-only: on BOTH samples Box 8 (the property securing the mortgage, in WA) differs from the borrower address (NC) — these are RETAINED / non-owner-occupied properties, so the 1098 evidences the housing expense (Box 1 interest + Box 10 taxes) and the debt balance (Box 2) on a retained property, which DT-6 reads. This is better than the plan assumed (it framed the type as processor-visibility); form_1098 has a real DT-6 tie.

PII: borrower_tin_masked registered (SSN, pre_masked=true — last-4 only). account_number reuses the existing global 'account_number' (ACCOUNT, from_raw) registration — masked display + a value-hash join to the loan's other documents. lender_tin is NOT masked — an EIN is a business identifier (LP-457), and its hyphenated format is guard-safe.
No nested list — a 1098 is flat (one property per form; Box 9 is a count).
